out.reading: Nothing unusual this morning, and the mild showers mean the seed is unlikely to be dug up by much more than the usual birds. The field is new-sown, so the seed is most exposed to rooks, pigeons and hares now, before the corn is up.
out.notes: Day 1 of spring sowing: keep the scarecrow up on the field, it costs almost nothing. Keep the children off bird-scaring unless birds are seen digging the seed. Watch for rooks and pigeons working the rows and for hare runs at the field edges. A snare set at the field edge is cheap and may take hares before they reach the young corn. Check the seed rows each morning.

out.notes: Spring sowing, day 2 of 8. Scarecrow stays up (it has worked; birds kept off). Keep one snare at the field edge where hare runs were seen; it costs one unit.
